/-!
# Erdős Problem 830

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/830](https://www.erdosproblems.com/830)
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped ArithmeticFunction.sigma
open Filter Real

namespace Erdos830

open scoped Classical in
/--
Let $A(x)$ count the number of amicable pairs $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$.
-/
noncomputable abbrev A (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ((Finset.Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ ×ˢ Finset.Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊).filter fun (a, b) ↦ a ≤ b ∧ IsAmicable a b).card

/-- **Erdos Problem 830, Part 1**
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$. Are there
infinitely many amicable pairs?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_830.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ {(a, b) | IsAmicable a b}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- **Erdos Problem 830, Part 2**
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then is it true that
$$A(x) > x^{1-o(1)}?$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_830.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ o : ℝ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ x in atTop,
    x ^ (1 - o x) < A x := by
  sorry

/--
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that $A(x) = o(x)$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_830.variants.erdos : A =o[atTop] id := by
  sorry

/--
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that
$A(x) \leq x \exp(-(\log x)^{1/3})$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_830.variants.pomerance : ∀ᶠ x in atTop, A x ≤ x * rexp (- Real.nthRoot 3 x.log) := by
  sorry

/--
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that
$A(x) \leq x \exp(-(\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1))(\log x\log\log x)^{1/2})$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_830.variants.pomerance_stronger :
    ∃ o : ℝ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ x in atTop, A x ≤ x * rexp (- (1/ 2 + o x) * √(x.log * x.log.log)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos830

findings.description: This declaration is tagged `research solved` and attributed to Pomerance [Po15]. It asserts `∃ o, o =o[atTop] 1 ∧ ∀ᶠ x in atTop, A x ≤ x * rexp (-(1/2 + o x) * √(log x * log (log x)))`, i.e. A(x) ≤ x·exp(−(½+o(1))·√(log x · log log x)). Pomerance's theorem instead has √(log x · log log log x), a triple logarithm. For large x, log log x > log log log x ≥ 0. So the Lean statement is strictly stronger than the proven result. I proved in Lean (scratch file) that the file's statement implies the triple-log version with the same `o`. The converse would need an extra saving of exp(−(½+o(1))(√(log x·log log x) − √(log x·log log log x))), which beats every power of log x. No such improvement is known: Pomerance 2015 is the best published bound. So the declaration asserts an unproven bound as a solved result, rather than Pomerance's theorem. Someone trying to prove it from the literature could not. The docstring has the same formula. Both copy a typo in the erdosproblems.com/830 remarks, which write $(\log x\log\log x)^{1/2}$ where the cited paper has $\log x\log\log\log x$.
findings.source_evidence: C. Pomerance, 'On amicable numbers', in Analytic Number Theory (in honor of H. Maier's 60th birthday), Springer 2015, pp. 321–327; author's version at https://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/amicablesv3.pdf. Theorem 1.1: 'As x → ∞, we have #A(x) ≤ x/exp((1/2 + o(1))√(log x log log log x))'. Here A(x) is the set of n ≤ x that belong to an amicable pair. The PDF typesets the radicand as `log x` followed by three `log` glyphs (width 41.517 = 3 × 13.839) and then `x`. Double logs such as `2x log log x` in the same PDF use two glyphs (27.678). The proof sets L = exp(½√(log x log log log x)). Step (vii) uses Lemma 2.1, S(x,y) ≤ x·exp(−(1+o(1))u log log u), and gets u ≥ (½+o(1))√(log x / log log log x), 'so that u log log u = (½+o(1))√(log x log log log x) = (1+o(1)) log L'. That balance only works with the triple log. The published abstract (https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-319-22240-0_19) gives the simplified corollary '#A(x) ≤ x/e^{√log x} for all sufficiently large x'. By contrast, the erdosproblems.com/830 remark (Wayback snapshot 2026-07-09; page last edited 28 Sep 2025) reads: 'later [Po15] to A(x) ≤ x exp(−(½+o(1))(log x log log x)^{1/2})'.
findings.suggested_fix:
Replace `√(x.log * x.log.log)` with `√(x.log * x.log.log.log)` and update the docstring to $A(x) \leq x \exp(-(\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1))(\log x\log\log\log x)^{1/2})$:

theorem erdos_830.variants.pomerance_stronger :
    ∃ o : ℝ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ x in atTop, A x ≤ x * rexp (- (1/ 2 + o x) * √(x.log * x.log.log.log)) := by
  sorry

This compiles. Pomerance's theorem implies it, because the pair count `A x` is at most half the number of amicable n ≤ x. The erdosproblems.com remark could also be reported upstream for correction.

reformulations.difference: `A` filters on `a ≤ b ∧ IsAmicable a b`. `IsAmicable` includes `ne : a ≠ b`, so `A` counts pairs with a < b ≤ ⌊x⌋. Read literally, the source's definition ('σ(a)=σ(b)=a+b', counting '1 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ x') would also count (n, n) for every perfect number n ≤ x.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The source's 'amicable pair' links to Wikipedia's definition ('two different natural numbers'). Pomerance [Po15] also defines an amicable pair as 'two different positive integers a, b with s(a)=b, s(b)=a'. So requiring distinctness is the intended meaning. Even under the literal reading, the two counts differ by P(x), the number of perfect numbers ≤ x. P(x) = x^{o(1)} (Hornfeck–Wirsing; already P(x) < √x by Hornfeck). Hence A_lit(x) > x^{1−o(1)} ⟺ A(x) > x^{1−o(1)} (part ii), and A_lit = o(x) ⟺ A = o(x). The two Pomerance-type upper bounds are true under both readings, since the proven bounds (e.g. x/e^{√log x}) leave ample room to absorb P(x). Note that `a ≤ b` together with `a ≠ b` counts each unordered pair exactly once, as the source's a ≤ b does. Part i uses the same standard distinct-pair notion.

https://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/amicablesv3.pdf (C. Pomerance, On amicable numbers, 2015 — author's version; Theorem 1.1 and proof)
https://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/amicabletalk7.pdf (Pomerance, Amicable numbers, Brown seminar slides 2015: history of bounds incl. 1981 x/exp((log x)^{1/3}); Erdős heuristic x^{1-ε})
https://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/Amicable2.pdf (Pomerance 1981, J. reine angew. Math. 325 — scanned, text not extractable)
https://api.zbmath.org (record Zbl 1395.11017 for Pomerance 2015; summary unavailable)

review.notes:
What I checked per declaration.

- `A`: I proved in scratch that `Erdos830.A x = Acount ⌊x⌋₊` for a computable mirror. `#eval` gives A(283)=0, A(284)=1, A(1209)=1, A(1210)=2, matching the pairs (220,284) and (1184,1210). For x < 1, A(x) = 0.
- `parts.i`: `{(a, b) : ℕ × ℕ | IsAmicable a b}.Infinite` is faithful. Pairs with 0 cannot occur, since σ 1 0 = 0 forces b = 0 = a, which contradicts `ne`.
- `parts.ii`: `∃ o =o 1, ∀ᶠ x, x^(1 - o x) < A x` is the standard encoding of A(x) > x^{1−o(1)} for all large x. Pomerance's slides give Erdős's heuristic in the same form ('more than x^{1−ε} of them up to x, for each fixed ε > 0 and x sufficiently large').
- `variants.erdos` and `variants.pomerance`: both faithful and proven. The exact wording of the 1981 theorem is in a scanned PDF I could not read, but the Lean statement follows anyway from Pomerance 2015 (#amicable n ≤ x is at most x/e^{√log x}) plus the fact that the pair count is at most half of that.

The single finding is a typo on erdosproblems.com that was carried into the Lean. The site writes (log x log log x)^{1/2} where Pomerance's Theorem 1.1 has log x · log log log x. If maintainers kept the site's formula instead, the statement is not a known theorem, so the `research solved` tag would be wrong. The right fix is to add the third log.

Status: both parts are recorded as OPEN on erdosproblems.com (snapshot 2026-07-09) and in the teorth database, which matches the file.

Git log shows earlier fix commits to this file; I read only their titles, not the diffs.

not_demonstrated.reason: The statement is an asymptotic bound over the reals whose truth is unknown. It is stronger than Pomerance's proven bound (log log x where he has log log log x), but it isn't known to be false. A proof would need new mathematics beyond Pomerance 2015. A disproof would need lower bounds on amicable pairs that would settle part i, which is open. No small case decides it. The defect can only be documented against the primary source (Pomerance 2015, Theorem 1.1 and the definition of L in its proof); a few-line Lean proof can't show it.

submission.summary: I couldn't write a trivial proof or disproof, so there is no trivial_proof.lean. The one finding: `erdos_830.variants.pomerance_stronger` has √(log x·log log x), copied from a typo on erdosproblems.com. Pomerance's 2015 Theorem 1.1 has √(log x·log log log x). Because the file's version is stronger than anything proven and its truth is unknown, no short Lean proof or refutation exists. The evidence is the source itself: the theorem's typeset formula, the definition L = exp(½√(log x log log log x)) in the proof, and step (vii) of the proof, which only balances with a triple log. The suggested fix (add `.log` to get `x.log.log.log`) compiles. The checkout under /opt/formal-conjectures is unchanged. `lakefile.toml` and `run/` show up as modified in `git status`, but they date from before my session and belong to the sandbox setup.
submission.gave_up_reason: The only misformalization I reported is `Erdos830.erdos_830.variants.pomerance_stronger`. It is an asymptotic upper bound over the reals: A(x) ≤ x·exp(−(½+o(1))√(log x·log log x)). Its truth is unknown, so it has no short, honest proof or disproof. The defect is that it is strictly stronger than the proven result, Pomerance 2015 (which has log log log x). It is not known to be false, so it is not refutable either. Proving it would need a new improvement on the bound for amicable numbers. Disproving it would need a lower bound on the number of amicable pairs, which would settle the open infinitude question (part i). A `∀ᶠ x in atTop` bound gives nothing to compute or `decide`. My scratch lemma shows only that the file's statement implies the corrected triple-log statement. It shows nothing false or trivially true, so it doesn't qualify as a demonstration. I never created /workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean, so there was nothing to delete.

submission.summary:
I fixed `Erdos830.erdos_830.variants.pomerance_stronger` so it states Pomerance's 2015 Theorem 1.1. The bound now has `√(x.log * x.log.log.log)`, i.e. √(log x · log log log x). Before, it had a double log copied from a typo on erdosproblems.com. That version is stronger than any proven result, so the `research solved` tag was wrong for it.

The docstring now gives the same formula and cites [Po15, Theorem 1.1]. I also added a `[Po15]` reference entry to the module docstring. The `research solved` category and `AMS 11` tag stay as they were; they are correct for the corrected statement. No other declaration changed.

The file compiles with `lake env lean --json`. The only diagnostics are the five existing `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings, one per theorem. That still holds with the lakefile's problem-file linters and the line-length check turned on. The website's typo should also be reported to erdosproblems.com.
